### Shipping

Own what lands: verify each PR independently, land only the verified run from the root, then keep your hands off the stack. The main session runs every merge; workers return verdicts and evidence.

1. **Confirm authority, then verify each PR independently before it lands.** Merge only on the owner's explicit request (merge, land, ship, merge when ready) or a `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-full.md` grant that covers this queue. `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-stack.md` never reaches this playbook. One verifier worker per PR runs the change the way a user would through the project's `verify-<app>` skill (`skill://verify` creates it; a surface that cannot be driven here is reported "not drivable here"), parent against head, and returns `PASS`, `PASS+NOTES`, or `FAIL` in its final answer with the head SHA it ran. Only a verdict from a non-author counts, because an author checks what it meant to build: use a reviewer of a different tier from the author where possible (a vendor-diverse seat is not available, so a different tier and a different agent is the diversity). Green CI and an approving bot review are not verdicts, because neither runs the change as a user would. A verifier never pushes, replies on the PR, or merges; the main session records each verdict, head SHA, and patch-id in the queue file (`.omp/plans/<name>.md`).
2. **Land only the contiguous verified run rooted at the bottom.** Walk up from the lowest unmerged PR and stop at the first one without `PASS` or `PASS+NOTES`. The PRs below it are the run, and the top one is the ceiling. A verified PR above an unverified one waits, because it cannot land without the code below it. One whose branch neither holds nor needs that code can move onto trunk and land on its own, after a fresh verdict, because its old one ran with that code beneath it and trunk does not have it.
3. **Re-check that each verdict still describes the code.** A verdict covers a patch, and a chain rebase moves every PR above it to a new SHA without failing any check. Compute the patch with `git diff $(git merge-base <parent> <sha>) <sha> | git patch-id --stable` at the verdict SHA and at the current head, and compare before trusting an older verdict. When the patches differ only in tests, docs, or lint config, a lane's result stands if what it ran builds the same at both SHAs apart from noise. Noise is a difference that also shows up between two builds of the verdict SHA, or an embedded commit SHA. Report each kind of noise with its files, so a reader can check the call. The change itself still gets fresh checks and a review, because the old verdict never saw it. A lane with no build output, such as a dev server, cannot show this, so rerun it and re-verify anything else that drifted.
4. **Land bottom-up, one PR at a time, from the main session.** Always merge the run's lowest unmerged PR with `gh pr merge <pr> --squash`. A PR whose base is still its parent's branch merges into that branch, not trunk. After every merge read the state back with `gh pr view <pr> --json state,mergedAt,baseRefName`, because a merge command can report success when a merge queue only queued the PR, and a requested auto-merge is not a merge. A landed PR reads `MERGED` with trunk as its base, not its parent's branch. Arm `--auto` only on a PR whose verdict covers its current head, because it lands whatever head is ready. After a merge lands, retarget the PR whose base was the merged branch with `gh pr edit <pr> --base <trunk>`, move its patch onto the merge result (`git rebase --onto <trunk> <old-parent-tip> <branch>`), and push with `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<last-pushed-sha>`. The verdict covers the patch, not its commits, so step 3's patch-id rule decides whether it survives. Merge it once its checks pass and its verdict survives.
5. **Leave the stack alone while it lands.** Step 4's move of the next PR is the only change to a branch or base, because a merge lands whatever its branch and base hold at that moment, verdict or not. Watch the run with `~/.omp/agent/skills/ulw/scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr --queued-stack --stack-prs <bottom-to-top>` as a background bash job (`timeout: 0`; exit codes in `skill://ulw/playbooks/babysit.md` step 6) until it reports `COMPLETE` (exit 0) at the ceiling. A base that moves to trunk when its parent merges is expected, not damage to repair. If a merge stalls, find out why before you change anything.
6. **Stop at the ceiling.** Extending the run takes new verdicts, so it is a new pass through step 1.

Reply. In Korean, plain text: the verified run and its ceiling, each PR's verdict and which worker produced it, what landed and the `gh pr view` read-back that confirms it, and what the next gap needs.
